items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: We left Red Norvo’s band to go with Claude Thornhill’s band. ... But still Claude gave me a free hand, and he paid more money too.

ctx.x: Did you like being on the road?

I loved parts of it. And when I first left home with the Dick Stabile scene, I was so homesick, but then I outgrew it. You know you’d get to be buddies with the guys you worked with, and they’re like a family. I roomed with Conrad for two and a half years. We left Red Norvo’s band to go with Claude Thornhill’s band. We left together. And then when we left several others, Barry Gallbraith and Ted Goddard and a few others from that great little band left, actually we broke up the band, which for the moment Red…
Boy I’ve heard that name a lot, Schribman.
